title: GIANT GEM(Beta) v2.1 : All other ancestries, region (+-500K), p-value (<=0.05)
bodyHtml:
The GIANT Genomic Region Miner (GEM) is an in-development module that allows you to explore, filter, and prioritize genetically associated variants, credible sets, and tissue-specific epigenomic annotations across a region, providing decision support for prioritization of variants and genes for further research.

All genomic coordinates are in the hg19 (GRCh37) genome build.

The current GIANT GEM is a beta version. (Last update: Aug 31, 2022)

  • Please clean the cache of the browser if GIANT GEM isn't functioning correctly.
  • Start by choosing a phenotype. Start typing a keyword in the Phenotype field, then select a phenotype from the drop-down list.
  • Then set a genomic region: either enter a region in the format 'chromosome_number:start_coordinate-end_coordinate' (e.g., 8:117912512-118238953) or enter a gene name to set the region to the coordinates of that gene.
  • To change or add phenotypes, choose another phenotype in the Phenotype field as above, and then make a selection from the "Compare data" menu:
    • 'New search' removes the data on the page and initiates a new search.
    • 'Only overlapping' displays association plots for each phenotype and a "Combined" plot showing variants that are significantly associated with all added phenotypes. Only the shared variants are added to the table below.
    • 'All' displays association plots for each phenotype and a plot with all variants that are associated with all added phenotypes. All variants are added to the table below.
    • Associations can be compared by phenotype, sex, and ancestries.
  • To filter the variants by their overlap with tissue-specific epigenomic annotations, click "Filter associated variants by annotations". To guide your selection of annotation types and tissues, the Global Enrichment plot on the right shows you which tissue-specific annotations are enriched genome-wide for genetic associations with the selected phenotype. Select an annotation type, then select one or more tissues. The variant table is filtered to display only those variants located within annotations of the selected type in the selected tissue. You may make multiple selections of annotation types and tissues.
  • View and select specific biosamples within each tissue category: after selecting annotation type(s) and tissue categories, click "Filter associated variants by biosamples" to see annotations for individual tissue and cell types within each category. Click on one or more tracks to further filter the table by annotations in the selected biosamples.
  • To filter the variants by their overlap with regions linked to genes, click "Filter associated variants by linked genes". View the data behind these links at CMDGA.
  • To mark individual variants with a star, click a star icon in the table, or click the star icon in the information popup for a specific variant on the region plot.

{
  "query": {
    "type": "array",
    "format": [
      "phenotype",
      "ancestry",
      "region"
    ],
    "index": "associations"
  },
  "parameters": [
    {
      "parameter": "phenotype",
      "label": "Phenotype",
      "type": "list",
      "values": [
        "BMI_GIANT",
"HEIGHT_GIANT",
"WHRadjBMI_female_GIANT",
"WHRadjBMI_GIANT",
"WHRadjBMI_male_GIANT",
"WHRU_female_GIANT",
"WHRU_GIANT",
"WHRU_male_GIANT"
      ]
    },
    {
      "parameter": "ancestry",
      "label": "Ancestry",
      "type": "list",
      "values": [
        "AA",
        "EA",
        "HS",
        "SA",
        "EU"
      ]
    },
    {
      "parameter": "region",
      "label": "Region (gene +-500K)",
      "type": "input",
      "values": "kp genes",
      "convert to region": "true",
      "expand region": "true",
      "expand region by": 1000000
    }
  ]
}

dataTableLegendHtml:
The table below displays genetic associations and annotations for the variants in this region. The default view shows all associated variants. As you add criteria, the table is filtered. Click on a column header to sort by that column. Mouse over a column header for more information. If 2 or more phenotypes are selected, the table cells are color-coded by phenotype. After adding epigenomic annotations or target gene links, click the "View" button to see detailed evidence.

If you select multiple annotation types and/or multiple tissues, you can use the "Compare annotated regions" menu to see how they overlap. Setting this menu to "And" displays in the Annotation overlap column the coordinates of the region representing the intersection of all annotated regions that overlap a variant, and also filters the table to those variants that are present in all selected annotated regions. Setting the menu to "Or" displays the coordinates of the union of all regions, and displays all variants that are in at least one of the selected annotated regions.
dataVisualizerLegendHtml: Linkage disequilibrium (LD) values in the association plot are drawn from the 1000 Genomes reference panel via the Michigan Imputation Server. The LD plot on the right shows only variants for which LD information is available.
